newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ben & Jerry's sees Benelux break-even in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Ben & Jerry's sees Benelux break-even in 1998.

text.p: U.S. Nasdaq-quoted ice cream company Ben & Jerry's, which entered the Belgian market on Monday, said it was aiming for a break-even in the three-country Benelux region next year.
"We expect to operate at break-even by 1998," said Rens Groeneveld, head of operations of Ben & Jerry's Benelux.

The company, which aims to blend the sale of ice cream with the promotion of social improvement, was first launched in the Benelux in the Netherlands last year and is currently available there at about 450 outlets.
Depending on the level of succes in Belgium, the brand could be launched in Luxembourg in a year's time.

In Belgium, Ben & Jerry's will initially sell eight of a palette of 50 flavours at supermarkets of retailer Delhaize and the White Night network of night shops, at 190 francs ($5.33) per half litre pot.
Groeneveld, who described the Belgian market as "the den of the ice cream tastebuds", said Ben & Jerry's had no immediate plans for a major advertising campaign.

Ben & Jerry's, which has a total turnover of $170 million and staff of more than 700, has also opened two "scoop shops" in the Netherlands -- in Amsterdam and Delft -- but Groeneveld was unable to say when such shops would be opened in Belgium.

Ben & Jerry's, whose ice cream is imported directly from the company's Vermont headquarters and is also available in France and the United Kingdom, donates 7.5 percent of pre-tax earnings to socially-oriented projects.
It has allowed the Human Rights Watch organisation to acquire 15 percent of the shares in its Benelux operations.
The brand competes in the super-premium high quality ice cream range with Haagen-Dazs, which falls in the same price category and has a market share of more than 50 percent.
Groeneveld said Ben & Jerry's has 45 percent of the U.S. market in the super premium segment but added he was unable to assess the market share in the Netherlands.
